screening_decisions.reason: Randomized trial comparing WBC-reduced vs standard platelet concentrates in acute leukemia patients. While primary outcome is alloimmunization/refractoriness, this relates to transfusion efficacy which impacts bleeding prevention.
Randomized trial of ABO-matched vs mismatched platelet transfusions in acute leukemia patients. Evaluates transfusion efficacy (CCI) which relates to bleeding prevention.
Systematic review and meta-analysis, not a primary RCT. Does not meet study design criteria.
Retrospective review of 2942 patients, not a randomized controlled trial. Does not meet study design criteria.
Prospective comparative study where centers decided which trigger to use (10/nl vs 20/nl). Not a randomized trial - allocation was by center choice, not random assignment.

Randomized trial comparing low, medium, and high doses of prophylactic platelet transfusions in patients undergoing hematopoietic stem-cell transplantation or chemotherapy for hematologic cancers. Primary endpoint was bleeding grade 2 or higher.
Abstract describes observational relationship between platelet count and hemorrhage. No indication of randomization. Does not meet study design criteria.
Observational analysis of transfusion practice patterns over 9 months. Not a randomized controlled trial.
Secondary analysis of the SPRINT RCT comparing photochemically treated vs conventional platelets. Includes bleeding outcomes and transfusion requirements in thrombocytopenic patients.
Review article discussing controversies in platelet transfusion therapy. Not a primary research study or RCT.
Retrospective analysis of 18,706 patient days in chronic SAA patients. Not a randomized controlled trial.
Prospective randomized trial comparing UVB-irradiated vs control platelet concentrates in patients with hematologic malignancy (mainly AML). Assesses transfusion efficacy and alloimmunization.
Prospective comparative trial where participating centers decided which trigger to use (10 vs 20 x 10^9/L). Not randomized - allocation was by center choice.
Study involves patients with ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm (vascular surgery), not patients with haematological disorders. Wrong population per selection criteria.
Randomized crossover study comparing buffy coat-derived vs PRP-derived platelet concentrates in multitransfused hematologic patients. Evaluates adverse reactions and corrected increments.
Prospective study comparing ABO-identical vs mismatched platelets in children. Abstract does not indicate randomization - appears to be observational comparison of available transfusions.
Randomized controlled trial comparing plasma-removed vs prestorage WBC-reduced platelets in adults with hematologic malignancies. Evaluates acute reaction frequency.
Prospective randomized trial comparing centrifugation vs filtration for leukocyte depletion in platelet concentrates for acute leukemia patients. Evaluates alloimmunization and refractoriness.

Controlled randomized double-blinded trial (euroSPRITE) comparing photochemically treated vs conventional platelet components in thrombocytopenic patients. Assesses hemostasis and hemorrhagic adverse events.
Retrospective cohort study estimating costs of chemotherapy-induced thrombocytopenia. Not a randomized controlled trial.

This study compares two platelet concentrate preparations (BC-PC vs SD-PC) in 32 patients with haematological malignancies, but the abstract does not describe randomization. It appears to be an observational/comparative study rather than an RCT.

Randomized prospective study with 75 female patients with hematologic malignancies (mostly acute leukemia). Patients were randomized to receive standard vs leukocyte-depleted platelet transfusions. While the primary focus is on alloimmunization, this is an RCT involving prophylactic platelet transfusions in haematological disorders.
This is a review/overview article discussing various trials and controversies in platelet transfusion practice. It is not an RCT itself.
This is explicitly described as a 'retrospective analysis' comparing two time periods (1997-1998 vs 1999-2001) with different trigger levels. It is not a randomized controlled trial.

Phase II crossover study in 32 patients with thrombocytopenia, but the abstract does not specify that patients have haematological disorders. The population may include non-haematological causes of thrombocytopenia.
This is a national audit examining compliance with transfusion guidelines across 187 UK hospitals. It is an observational audit study, not an RCT.

Randomized controlled trial with 111 patients with acute leukemia or undergoing autologous PBPC transplantation. Patients were randomly assigned to receive low-dose (3 units) or standard-dose (5 units) prophylactic platelet transfusions. Monitored daily for bleeding events.
This is a systematic review/methodological paper examining how bleeding outcomes are documented and analyzed in transfusion studies. It is not an RCT.
This is a quality control/surveillance study analyzing bacterial contamination rates in 1,004,206 platelet donations. It is not an RCT involving patient transfusions.

Multicentre, open-label, randomized, non-inferiority trial with 278 evaluable patients. Compared buffy-coat derived leukoreduced platelet concentrates stored in plasma vs PASIII with/without pathogen reduction. Included bleeding as a secondary endpoint.

Randomized, controlled, double-blinded trial with 201 patients (101 A-PC, 100 C-PC). Patients were randomized to receive conventional PC or amotosalen-treated PC. Bleeding was assessed as a secondary endpoint.
This is a narrative review of the literature examining platelet dosing for prophylactic transfusions. It is not an RCT.

Prospective randomized study in patients with hematologic malignancy (mainly acute myeloid leukemia). Patients were randomly assigned to receive UVB-irradiated or control PCs. Assessed transfusion efficacy and alloimmunization.
This study involves neonatal intensive care unit patients, not patients with haematological disorders. Additionally, it uses a before-after design rather than randomization.

Randomized study with 60 allogeneic haematopoietic progenitor cell transplant recipients. Patients were randomized to receive platelets stored 1-5 days vs 6-7 days. Assessed corrected count increments and bleeding events.
This is a meta-analysis summarizing results from five RCTs. It is a secondary analysis, not a primary RCT.
While donors were randomized to receive thrombopoietin or placebo, the abstract does not clearly state that recipients were randomized. The study design for patient allocation is unclear.
This is a clinical practice guideline document from ASCO, not an RCT.
This is a review article summarizing recent evidence regarding platelet transfusions in haematology patients. It is not an RCT.

Double-blind randomized controlled trial with 119 analyzed patients. Thrombocytopenic adults requiring prophylactic platelet transfusion were randomly allocated to standard-dose or low-dose platelets. Primary outcome was WHO bleeding grade >= 2.

This is a prospective randomized clinical trial comparing two prophylactic platelet transfusion thresholds (10K vs 20K) in HSCT recipients. Meets all criteria: RCT design, platelet concentrates, haematological disorder population (HSCT), and prophylactic transfusion for bleeding prevention.

This is a prospective dose-response study where each patient received multiple doses sequentially (within-subject design), not a randomized controlled trial comparing independent groups. Does not meet the RCT criterion.
This is a prospective observational study with retrospective analysis of reticulated platelet markers. Not a randomized controlled trial. Does not meet the RCT criterion.
This is a systematic review, not a primary RCT. While it includes some RCTs in its analysis, the study itself is a review article and does not meet the RCT criterion.
This is a prospective observational study evaluating appropriateness of platelet transfusion requests. Not a randomized controlled trial. Does not meet the RCT criterion.

This is a randomized cross-over study comparing autologous cryopreserved platelets vs allogeneic fresh platelets in patients with chemotherapy-induced thrombocytopenia. Meets RCT criterion, uses platelet concentrates, and addresses prophylactic transfusion for bleeding prevention in cancer patients receiving chemotherapy.
This is a single-arm prospective study comparing a therapeutic transfusion protocol to a historical control group. Not a randomized controlled trial. Does not meet the RCT criterion.
This is a review article about platelet-endothelial cell interactions. Not a primary research study or RCT. Does not meet any inclusion criteria.
This is a retrospective analysis of data from cardiac surgery patients (CABG). Wrong population (cardiac surgery, not haematological disorders) and wrong study design (retrospective, not RCT).

While this is an RCT, it evaluates premedication to prevent transfusion reactions (NHTR), not prophylactic platelet transfusion for bleeding prevention. The intervention is not platelet transfusion itself.

This is a prospective randomized controlled trial comparing ABO-identical vs ABO-unmatched platelet transfusions in patients with haematological diseases. Meets all criteria: RCT design, platelet concentrates, haematological disorder population, and prophylactic transfusion context.

This references the Slichter et al. NEJM 2010 study, which is a well-known RCT comparing different doses of prophylactic platelet transfusions for bleeding prevention in thrombocytopenic patients. Despite limited abstract text, the title indicates it meets the criteria.
This study investigates causes of febrile transfusion reactions (plasma vs cellular components), not prophylactic platelet transfusion for bleeding prevention. Wrong outcome focus.

This is a prospective before-and-after study comparing 20K vs 10K thresholds over two time periods. Not a randomized controlled trial (no randomization between groups). Does not meet the RCT criterion.
This is a mathematical modeling study with chart review validation. Not a randomized controlled trial. Does not meet the RCT criterion.

This is a prospective randomized trial comparing HLA-matched vs mismatched single-donor platelet transfusions in cancer patients with therapy-induced thrombocytopenia. Meets RCT criterion, uses platelet concentrates, and addresses prophylactic transfusion for bleeding prevention.

This is a randomized controlled trial comparing ABO-matched vs ABO-mismatched platelet transfusions in patients with acute leukaemia or Hodgkin's lymphoma. Meets all criteria: RCT design, platelet concentrates, haematological disorder population, and prophylactic transfusion context.

This study evaluates bleeding risk during CVC placement, not prophylactic platelet transfusion for bleeding prevention. The conclusion is that prophylactic correction is NOT necessary. Wrong intervention/outcome focus.
While this is an RCT with prophylactic platelet transfusion, the population is patients undergoing massive transfusion (trauma/surgical), not patients with haematological disorders. Wrong population.
This is a methodology/design paper describing how to conduct clinical trials, not actual trial results. Not a primary RCT with results. Does not meet the RCT criterion.
This is an annotation/review article that reviews evidence for platelet transfusion thresholds and discusses unresolved issues. It is not a primary research study or RCT.
This is an animal study using rabbits to examine endothelial changes with electron microscopy. It is not a human RCT involving platelet transfusions in patients with haematological disorders.

This is an RCT comparing pathogen-reduced platelets vs reference platelets in patients with chemotherapy-induced thrombocytopenia. While the abstract doesn't explicitly specify haematological disorders, the conservative approach warrants inclusion as the population may include haematological patients. The study involves prophylactic platelet transfusions.

This is an RCT comparing fresh vs stored single donor platelet concentrates in patients undergoing allogeneic bone marrow transplantation. BMT recipients are patients with haematological disorders, and the study involves prophylactic platelet transfusions.

This is a derivation/validation study developing a clinical prediction rule (Bleeding Risk Index) using logistic regression analysis. It is not an RCT. Additionally, it includes patients with solid tumors, not exclusively haematological disorders.

This is an observational study measuring platelet survival using 51Cr labeling in patients with bone marrow failure. It is not an RCT and does not involve platelet transfusion interventions being tested.
This is an RCT testing recombinant human thrombopoietin (rhTPO), not platelet transfusions. Additionally, the study population consists of patients with solid tumors, not haematological disorders.

This is a PROBE-design RCT comparing high vs standard dose prophylactic platelet transfusions in patients with acute leukemia or undergoing autologous hematopoietic stem cell transplantation. These are haematological disorders, and the study involves prophylactic platelet transfusions.

This is a phase II study testing ex vivo expanded megakaryocyte progenitor cells, not platelet transfusion strategies. While patients received platelet transfusions, the intervention being tested is the expanded cell product, not platelet transfusion protocols.
This is a prospective observational study comparing buffy-coat vs apheresis platelet concentrates. It is not an RCT.
This is a retrospective non-randomized comparative analysis comparing two time periods with different transfusion policies. It is not an RCT.
This is an animal study using rabbits to examine platelet function and survival. It is not a human RCT involving platelet transfusions in patients with haematological disorders.

This is an RCT comparing different prophylactic platelet transfusion triggers (10 vs 30 x 10^9/L) in allogeneic hematopoietic progenitor cell transplant recipients. These are patients with haematological disorders, and the study directly addresses prophylactic platelet transfusion for bleeding prevention.
This is an observational study evaluating a conservative transfusion approach in patients with gynecological cancers (solid tumors, not haematological disorders). It is not an RCT.
This is a national survey/statistical report on blood collection and transfusion practices in the US. It is not an RCT or clinical study.

This is an RCT comparing three types of platelet concentrates (single donor platelet-pheresis, buffy coat-derived, and platelet-rich plasma-derived) in patients with haematological malignancy. The study involves platelet transfusions in the target population.
This is a review article discussing platelet concentrate products, preparation methods, and transfusion guidelines. It is not an RCT or primary research study.

This is a secondary analysis from the TRAP (Trial to Reduce Alloimmunization to Platelets) multicenter RCT. The TRAP trial randomized patients with haematological malignancies to receive different platelet products. While this paper focuses on transfusion reactions, it is derived from an RCT involving prophylactic platelet transfusions in haematological patients. Conservative approach warrants inclusion.
This is a prospective observational analysis evaluating bleeding complications after implementing a stringent transfusion policy. It is not an RCT - it's a before/after or prospective cohort study.

This is a prospective randomized trial comparing prestorage WBC-reduced platelet concentrates vs standard platelet concentrates in autologous progenitor cell transplant patients. These are patients with haematological disorders, and the study involves platelet transfusions.
This is a critical review article summarizing methods for measuring bleeding severity, not an RCT of prophylactic platelet transfusion.
This is a professional consensus/guideline document presenting recommendations from AFSSaPS, not an RCT. The abstract explicitly states recommendations are \'not based on any randomized studies\'.

This study compares two dose levels of prophylactic platelet transfusions (low vs high dose) in thrombocytopenic patients with acute leukemia. While the abstract does not explicitly state \'randomized\

While this is an RCT in patients with hematologic malignancy receiving platelet support, the primary outcome is HLA alloimmunization, not bleeding prevention. The intervention (bedside leucodepletion) focuses on preventing alloimmunization rather than optimizing prophylactic transfusion for bleeding prevention.

This is an observational study of platelet transfusion utilization in general medical-surgical ICU patients, not specifically patients with haematological disorders undergoing chemotherapy or stem cell transplantation. The study design is retrospective/observational, not an RCT.

This is a randomized study comparing single-donor vs multiple-donor platelets in patients with acute leukemia, but the primary outcomes are alloimmunization and refractoriness, not bleeding prevention. The study does not address the effectiveness of prophylactic transfusion for preventing bleeding.

This is an RCT comparing plasma removal vs WBC reduction to prevent transfusion reactions in adults with hematologic disease. The primary outcome is transfusion reactions (fever, etc.), not bleeding prevention. The intervention targets reaction prevention rather than bleeding prevention.
This is a duplicate/similar guideline document from AFSSAPS presenting expert recommendations, not an RCT. The abstract states recommendations are \'not based on any randomized studies\'.

This is a randomized crossover trial in children comparing plasma removal and WBC reduction, but the primary outcome is febrile nonhemolytic transfusion reactions (FNHTRs), not bleeding prevention. The study does not evaluate bleeding outcomes.

This is an RCT in 56 children with acute leukemia comparing prophylactic platelet transfusion (threshold 20,000/mm3) vs therapeutic transfusion (only when bleeding occurs). The study directly addresses the review objective by evaluating bleeding outcomes (time to first bleeding, number of bleeding episodes, days with bleeding) in patients with haematological disorders.

This is an economic analysis/decision modeling study based on data from another trial, not a primary RCT. The study evaluates cost implications of platelet dose changes rather than clinical bleeding outcomes.

This is a methodology paper developing comprehensive criteria for assessing therapy-induced toxicity. It is not a clinical trial of platelet transfusion and does not involve patients with haematological disorders receiving prophylactic platelet transfusions.

This is a prospective observational analysis of platelet utilization practices at one hospital when transitioning transfusion triggers. It is not an RCT; there is no randomization or control group. The study describes practice patterns rather than testing an intervention.

This study compares two time periods (1989-1993 vs 1994-1998) with different transfusion thresholds in adult AML patients. This is a historical cohort/quasi-experimental design, not an RCT. Patients were not randomized to threshold groups.

This study compares three groups (leucocyte-poor components, standard components, and leucocyte-poor plus HLA-matched) for HLA alloimmunization outcomes. The primary outcome is alloimmunization, not bleeding prevention. The study design does not appear to be randomized.

This is a prospective, randomized, double-blind, multiple-crossover trial comparing lower-dose vs higher-dose apheresis platelet transfusions in 46 patients undergoing high-dose therapy followed by hematopoietic progenitor cell transplantation. The study evaluates prophylactic transfusion outcomes including platelet count increments and transfusion-free intervals, which relate to bleeding prevention. Population matches (patients undergoing stem cell transplantation).

This is a randomized single-institution trial comparing two prophylactic platelet transfusion thresholds (\\u226410,000/\\u03bcL vs \\u226420,000/\\u03bcL) in 78 patients undergoing induction therapy for acute leukemia. The study directly addresses the review objective by evaluating bleeding episodes, transfusion requirements, and morbidity outcomes in patients with haematological disorders receiving chemotherapy.

This is a large RCT (SPRINT Trial) with 645 thrombocytopenic patients randomly assigned to receive photochemically treated vs conventional platelets. The primary endpoint was WHO grade 2 bleeding during platelet support period. The study evaluates prophylactic platelet transfusion effectiveness for bleeding prevention, though the specific haematological disorder status of all patients is not fully detailed in the abstract.

This is a multicentre laboratory study evaluating the accuracy of haematology analysers for platelet counting in severe thrombocytopenia. It is not a clinical trial of platelet transfusion and does not involve patient outcomes related to bleeding prevention.

This is a double-blind randomized study in 18 patients with thrombocytopenia and acute leukemia comparing prophylactic platelet transfusion vs platelet-poor plasma. The study directly evaluates bleeding frequency as the outcome, affirming the value of prophylactic platelet transfusions. Population matches (acute leukemia patients) and intervention is prophylactic platelet transfusion.

This study focuses on preventing febrile nonhemolytic transfusion reactions (FNHTR) rather than preventing bleeding. While it involves platelet transfusions and includes patients with haematological disorders, the primary outcome is FNHTR incidence, not bleeding prevention. The intervention (leukocyte depletion) is aimed at reducing transfusion reactions, not at preventing thrombocytopenic bleeding.

This RCT involves platelet transfusions in patients with acute nonlymphocytic leukemia, but the primary objective is to determine whether leukocyte-depleted platelets can modify alloimmunization development, not to prevent bleeding. The primary outcome is lymphocytotoxic antibody (LCTAb) levels as a marker of alloimmunization. The study does not assess bleeding outcomes or prophylactic transfusion for bleeding prevention.

This is a prospective randomized study involving prophylactic platelet transfusions in 21 patients treated with intensive chemotherapy for hematologic malignancies. The study compares platelet concentrates prepared in plasma versus platelet additive solution (PAS-2). While the primary outcomes measured are reactions and corrected count increments (CCIs), the context is prophylactic transfusion for bleeding prevention in haematological disorders. The study meets the selection criteria as it involves RCT of platelet concentrates given prophylactically to patients with haematological disorders.

This study compares single-donor apheresis platelets (SDAP) versus pooled platelet concentrates (PPC) for prophylactic transfusions in 33 patients with AML/MDS receiving allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation. The transfusions are explicitly prophylactic (given when platelet count ≤15 x 10^9/L to prevent bleeding). The study measures platelet counts, corrected count increments, and hemorrhage episodes. This clearly meets the selection criteria as it is an RCT involving platelet concentrates given to prevent bleeding in patients with haematological disorders.

This is a guidelines document that summarizes evidence on platelet transfusion practices. It is not a primary research study or RCT. The selection criteria specifically require RCTs involving transfusions of platelet concentrates. Guidelines documents do not meet the study design criteria for inclusion in this systematic review.
